plan.title: Author the gate plan
plan.imperative: Map-first: BEFORE authoring execute.json, produce a mission frame from the map input the context step resolved, using templates/MISSION_FRAME.template.md (intent; affected capabilities; relevant examples/events; structural anchors; governing constraints/assumptions; decision anchors and decision pressure; claims/evidence surfaces; map confidence/staleness/disputes; out of scope). Write it to .agent-work/epic-559/c2-generate-the-spine/MISSION_FRAME.md — that exact path is what the c6 gate reads, so a frame parked anywhere else reads as no frame at all. For a trivial local/mechanical change where the map adds nothing, shrink or skip the frame and say so in its intent; c6 is waivable, so take that escape as a RECORDED waiver (<engine> waive plan --cond c6 --authority human --reason '...') rather than as a silent skip. The c6 gate runs map_orient.py verify-frame over that file: every anchor id the frame cites must exist in the map inventory the context step resolved, or — when context came back DEGRADED — must be one of the substitutes the receipt hash-pinned there, so the frame is compared against a committed prior declaration instead of a same-breath assertion. Know what that check is and is not, and do not overclaim it: it is a regression floor so map-IGNORING cannot silently return, not the fix for map-LATENESS. Measured against this epic's baseline five runs it has sensitivity 0/4 and specificity 0/1, and it inherits the late-anchor defect it was built next to, because anchors-in-a-late-frame is compliance without sequence. The load-bearing map-first anchor is at the context step ('before you open any source file'), which is why verify-orientation is gated there and verify-frame is gated only here. Do NOT 'fix' that asymmetry by also running verify-frame at context: no frame exists at context — the step runs before understand and plan — and the only way to make it pass there is to let an ABSENT frame pass, which is exactly the refusal the whole check is built on. If verify-frame ever has to be context-safe, give it a step-scoped mode; never a vacuous pass. For any low-confidence/stale/disputed map area the run depends on, alter the plan accordingly: add a scout/verification gate or surface it to the human as a decision — never author gates that silently trust an unverified map. Surface durable-structure choices as decision candidates per the skill's Decision candidates section rather than choosing alone. Then author the gate plan into execute.json: each gate the smallest reasonable bite, with close criteria, required evidence, and an anchors block cut from the frame. Before the plan-approved checkpoint run plan-alternatives (parallel gate-plan candidates under distinct constraints, via the references/design-it-twice-brief.md contract) and a cold plan critic (reads the candidate plan + mission frame only, no authoring context); both bias-to-yes — any skip is surfaced as a named untaken road — and the panel-vs-single choice is surfaced to the human at plan approval. Get the human to approve it. In delegated mode, satisfy c3 (plan approved) by attaching a user-decision evidence item citing the launch order's frozen plan and scope -- by default via the spine_evidence MCP tool (action=attach, task_id=plan, evidence_type=user-decision, fields={cite: 'LAUNCH_ORDER:Mission'}); CLI fallback: attach plan --type user-decision --field cite='LAUNCH_ORDER:Mission'; surface a plan-invalidating discovery to the Admiral rather than blocking on the human. See the commander skill's Delegated/autonomous mode.

execute.context_headroom_note: #467. Absolute-token context reserve for THIS gate only: the engine subtracts it from both the soft and hard caps before dividing by the model's window, so `execute` may not be BEGUN with less than this much room left below the hard cap. It makes the imperative's existing prose instruction ('ensure context headroom before entering') enforceable, and it can only ever tighten -- no gate can raise a threshold. WHY 30000, and it is a GUESS, revisable in place: `execute` is the run's longest gate and the one that cannot be abandoned halfway, because it drives every crew gate and each crew dispatch costs tens of thousands of tokens. The only observation available was a commander sitting at ~127K fill after a cold resume plus one full three-task gate -- which bounds one gate's marginal cost in the tens of thousands but cannot separate it from the resume baseline. 30K is a round number at the low end of that range: on claude-opus-5 (1M window, 80K soft / 150K hard) it moves execute's begin-work line from 15% to 12% and its advisory from 8% to 5%, while every other gate keeps the shipped default. The named settle experiment (read fill_fraction across completed commander runs at the moment execute was started) is NOT runnable from existing artifacts -- gauge.json keeps only the latest reading and the per-gate context manifests record no fill -- so a later run may revise this number here, in this one place, without re-deriving anything.

feedback.title: Record workflow feedback
feedback.imperative: Before committing, reflect honestly on how this run actually went: how closely you followed the skills, handoffs, and checklists; where you had to improvise or work around the instructions; what was ambiguous, missing, or contradictory; and what would have helped. Include the crew Workflow Feedback harvested at each gN-integrate. A 'none' answer requires a run-specific reason ('none — confirmed after review: <what you checked>'); a bare 'none' does not close this step. Then record what happened as EPISODES: one episode per distinct thing that happened — not one per run, and not a summary — each stating its task-intent, expected-behavior, observed-behavior, impact-cost and workaround. An episode is a record, not a rule: write what you observed, and do NOT write a rule for a future agent to follow — a rule to follow belongs in docs/agents/* and is a human's call. Write the delta to .agent-work/epic-559/c2-generate-the-spine/episode-delta.json and apply it deterministically: python /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/apply_episode_delta.py --delta .agent-work/epic-559/c2-generate-the-spine/episode-delta.json --store-root episodes. Pass --store-root on every invocation: the writer's default resolves relative to the installed skill directory, so an installed copy would silently build a store at ~/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/episodes — outside the repo — while every gate reported green. Never hand-edit a file under episodes/: that writer is the only write path into it. Then run the capture gate before advancing: python /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/verify_episode_captured.py epic-559/c2-generate-the-spine --store-root episodes --phase feedback.

archive.title: Archive, commit, and push
archive.imperative: Commit all remaining work, including this run's episodes under episodes/. That is a tracked repo-root path, so the committed episode IS the durable record: it survives `git worktree remove` and lands in a fresh clone. None of the old is-.agent-work-gitignored reasoning applies to it. Push the branch to remote. When you open a PR on Windows, write the body to a temp file and use gh pr create -F <file> — a bash heredoc and a PowerShell @'...'@ here-string both fail for gh pr create --body (here-strings work for git commit -m, not PR bodies). Move .agent-work/epic-559/c2-generate-the-spine/ to .agent-work/archive/<date>-epic-559/c2-generate-the-spine/. Run the archive-phase capture gate before marking archive complete — it additionally requires git to TRACK the episode, which is what proves the record outlived this worktree: python /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/verify_episode_captured.py epic-559/c2-generate-the-spine --store-root episodes --phase archive. Confirm the branch is clean and merge-ready per repo guidance. The engine mechanically refuses closeout (c4) when the staged diff includes suspicious artifacts (oversized files, generated record dumps, disallowed dirs, binary/blob additions, large data files); if any are intentional, a human waives c4 via <engine> waive archive --cond c4 --authority human --reason "..." rather than hand-editing the spine. Release the engine session lease only as your VERY LAST action, AFTER the archive postconditions pass and you have run the engine's final advance on archive (the advance that marks the spine done): by default call the spine_lease MCP tool with action=release (this is your own spine; the door needs no session id argument). CLI fallback: <engine> release --session-id commander-epic-559/c2-generate-the-spine. Release must come after that closing advance, never before it — the lease must cover every journaled action, so the release is the final journal entry; releasing earlier leaves archive's own closeout entries (attest/waive/advance) after the lease release and fails the terminal provenance check.

postconditions.statement: the work is REACHABLE: this branch has a pull request that is OPEN or MERGED. A merged PR is reachable work; a closed-unmerged one is not, and neither is no PR at all. A terminal spine and a pushed branch describe the run, not the ref -- CI never runs on an unopened branch, and every commander that reached a terminal spine without opening one had to be chased for it. Open the PR even if the work is unfinished; declare FINAL or PENDING in its title and hand the merge up. Two properties of the check text are load-bearing. The branch is derived at CHECK time from the repo root, never resolved at instantiation: init instantiates the spine before it starts the branch, so the branch need not exist yet -- and a literal branch placeholder is not a resolver-owned token, so instantiation cannot catch one and would ship it unsubstituted. The count is compared in the SHELL because the engine's verdict for a command condition is the EXIT CODE and stdout is discarded: gh --jq 'length > 0' prints true or false but exits 0 either way, so that form can never fail.

triage_candidates.statement: A Commander cannot drive its own execute.json through the MCP door. scripts/mcp_spine_server.py binds exactly one file at import time -- SPINE = Path(os.environ["SPINE_FILE"]).resolve() (line 106) -- and there is no per-call spine addressing, while the Commander spine's own `execute` step requires driving a SECOND checklist (execute.json) that the door cannot address. Under the human's categorical ruling ("anything that we want to do for the spine needs to be accessible via mcp... anything that we can only do via the cli is a defect") this is a defect, and it is the same family as the four unresolvable <engine> tokens the launch order already flags -- but deeper, because no token substitution fixes it: the door has no verb that can name a second file. Closest compliant thing done and reported as misfit: execute.json is driven through checklist_engine.py directly, with every call journaled to execute.json.journal, so the work is engine-driven and auditable even though it is not door-driven. Floated to the Admiral; fixing it is an mcp_spine_server.py change, outside a Commander's latitude.

scripts/recover_crews.py misclassifies a COMPLETED spine-only dispatch as NEEDS-ABANDON. Measured: run_crew.py judged constellation/epic-559/c2-generate-the-spine/g3-dispatch/spine-probe/attempt-2 "completed" on spine_terminal and wrote status=completed, completed_at set, result=None into crew-runs.json; recover_crews.py then reports "NEEDS-ABANDON -- not running and no result; require explicit --abandon ... --relaunch". Its classifier keys on a result artifact, which a spine-only dispatch deliberately does not have (run_crew's own --result is documented as optional when --spine is given, precisely because such a crew is judged on its spine reaching a terminal state instead). The consequence is the exact failure recover_crews exists to prevent: a resumed or relaunched Commander running the recovery check first, as doctrine requires, is told to abandon and relaunch a crew whose work is already finished and whose spine is already terminal with its lease released. The fix is to make classify_entry consult status=completed and/or the bound spine's terminal state when result is None and spine is set. Not fixed here -- outside this mission's scope.

why_trail.why: Work area was pre-scaffolded by the Admiral (LAUNCH_ORDER "Pre-empted Steps": init done, spine.json instantiated from COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json). I claimed the engine lease myself through the MCP door, and verified worktree isolation (verify_worktree_isolation.py --here exits 0: "worktree OK: in /home/tommy/projects/constellation-skills-wt/c2-generate-the-spine"). Noted for the record: init's imperative carries two of the four unresolvable `<engine>` CLI tokens the launch order flags as a defect in this spine — ignored per the human's ruling that the CLI is not agent-facing.

This repo carries no architecture map — map_orient probes five candidates and all five come back absent, unparseable or empty, so every commander here is structurally DEGRADED. I discharged it as a declared reading rather than pretending: six hash-pinned substitutes, the two unmapped gaps named (no packet map over checklist_engine.py/validate_spine.py/the spine-template corpus; no docs/agents/engine-config.json), and the scaffolding gap escalated to the Admiral as a triage candidate. The substitute that actually carries my mission's frame is docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md: it is the engine's on-disk contract, and it confirms the launch order's two load-bearing facts — `constraints` and `directives` are Task-level fields that `current` renders on the active gate (#420/#433), and `directives` legitimately carries both a dict-of-contracts shape and a flat list of strings. That is the substrate my generator must emit into, and I now have it from the schema rather than from the order's summary of it.

Reconciled the ask against the frozen launch order instead of interrogating (delegated mode), and checked the order's assumed baseline against the code rather than taking it on trust: no generator exists (tree-wide grep for generate_spine|spine_spec|spec_to_spine is empty), validate_spine.validate() is importable and its own docstring already names "a future spine generator" as its caller, and my own --sweep reproduces the order's baseline fault list exactly. The measurement that changes my design: `constraints` is not a free field — all 970 populated tasks and all three shipped-template instances use it to mean "rules this gate must respect", so beliefs/concerns/open questions do not belong there. `directives` means "a standing contract this gate must satisfy", is populated on only 22 tasks by four near-duplicate contracts, and renders as name + indented fields on the active gate. That is the field with room for a job, and it is where the handback substrate will go.

The plan I would have frozen after the design-it-twice panel was wrong in two places, and only running the engine found it. Three candidates converged on a hybrid — a pure translation function separated from every I/O act (C), a closed vocabulary of typed check kinds each with a generation-time probe keyed to one of the four historical defects (B), and an AST scan instead of a live import so generation never executes author-named code (C over B, which is defect 2's own shape one layer up). Then the cold panel took it apart: the `directives.handback` arrays I designed are unwritable — no engine verb appends to a `directives` field on an active gate, `amend rescope` touches pending gates only — so they would have rendered empty on every gate forever, which is "looks like it works" inside the mechanism built to avoid it. And the `user-decision` escalation I designed for a large claim can be attached and attested by the same session that made the claim, because `attach` takes no authority and stamps `produced_by: "engine"` for every caller, while `waive` three functions below it demands one. So the escalation could not fail against the agent it exists to check. Both are fixed: the handback contract now names the three verbs that actually persist (attach, flag-candidate, block) plus the recorded parent, and the escalation is now a review-result matching verdict APPROVE — a checked property, not bare arrival. The residual is not mine to close: the engine binds no provenance to evidence at all, so every user-decision checkpoint in the corpus is self-satisfiable, and that is floated to the Admiral rather than patched. The panel also cut the plan down — one file not two, five check kinds not seven, five gates not six — each on precedent I verified rather than on taste. My own execute.json validates OK with zero faults and zero undecidable, and carries the handback contract on every gate, which is the smallest honest dogfood available before the generator exists.

execute.json is driven to completion, and the two things worth carrying forward are both failures the run caught in its own machinery rather than successes. First: one of the mission's two non-optional properties was silently inert on every survey-type role spec, because record() evaluates only command-kind postconditions on a survey item and consolidate() reads only each item's result field. A cold reviewer found it by driving a generated survey to consolidation, not by reading it, and BLOCKED. The generator now refuses to inject a postcondition the engine will never consult and states the non-enforcement instead -- deliberately not taking the tempting command-check fix, which would have invented a convention with no producer and turned a gate that cannot fail into one that cannot pass, which is prior-wave verdict B's exact defect. Second: I authored a check omitting a required flag, the generator emitted it and the oracle accepted it, and only a real dispatch found it -- because the script probe verifies that flags an author NAMED exist and cannot see one they FAILED to name. That is the honest limit on the settling question and it is reported rather than softened. The run packet carries six classified discrepancies as evidence with none auto-filed, and verify_iterative_role_artifacts confirms it is G2-valid.

Reconciled directly because there is no packet map to hand a Cartographer, which the step itself names as the compliant path. The structural record here is map/INDEX.md, and the reconciliation that mattered was mechanical: a new module and then its extension each staled it, and both times the staleness surfaced as a red test rather than as anything anyone noticed while writing the code -- the authoring-side blind spot, twice, in one run. The judgement part went into docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md: the format is unchanged and now has its first producer, and the three engine behaviours this run measured are recorded with their consequences drawn rather than left implied -- especially that neither closing verb on a survey consults an artifact postcondition, which is a fact any future role spec has to plan around.

Six candidates routed, none filed, and the citation records the deferral rather than an approval — the launch order withheld filing authority explicitly, which is a different thing from authority being unclear. The two most valuable are both about the machinery the corpus uses to police itself rather than about my mission: recover_crews now advises abandoning and relaunching a spine-only crew whose work is already finished, which is precisely the duplication it exists to prevent; and a dispatched crew inherits its dispatcher's SPINE_FILE, so both my reviewers found the Commander's own spine bound in their environment and only their own doctrine stopped them driving it. I checked every candidate against the fix-now ladder rather than defaulting to defer — tc2 and tc5 are small enough to be tempting and both fail two rungs, and three of four does not qualify.

The run summary is written and it leads with what did not hold rather than with what did, because that is the more useful half. Property 2 is enforceable on a gated gate and not on a survey; the wrong-invocation class is narrowed and not closed, proven by a defect I authored myself that the generator emitted and the oracle accepted; and the generator cannot author a TDD-shaped plan at all, because a selector for a test that does not yet exist collects zero and the probe refuses it. The control pairing is in the report as three runs with their real output, including test ! -f proving nothing was written on the refusal and the corrected spec being written, because a refusal without the accepted half proves only that the guard fires. Six triage candidates routed to the Admiral with none filed, and three floats recorded rather than patched.

Eight episodes recorded, one per distinct thing that happened, each as a record and none as a rule for a future agent. The reflection is in COMMANDER_RETURN.md section 7 and notes-1.md, and it includes every crew's harvested Workflow Feedback rather than a bare none: two reviewers independently reported that their environment carried MY spine bound; the g1 implementer volunteered that it nearly shipped a guard fixture built on an unmeasured assumption about Path.glob and caught itself; the g2 crew flagged that the config path the design note's own example names does not exist. The capture itself produced a ninth thing worth recording in its own right: I wrote the `run` field kebab-cased, so the capture gate could not resolve the eight episodes it had just written. I did not hand-edit the store to fix it -- the writer is the only write path -- so the eight were retired with the reason stated and eight corrected ones created through the same writer. The gate now passes on the work-id verbatim.

Closeout, with one instruction deliberately not followed and the misfit reported rather than hidden. The imperative says to move .agent-work/epic-559/c2-generate-the-spine/ under .agent-work/archive/. I did not, for three reasons: the spine I am still driving lives in that directory, so moving it would break SPINE_FILE before this very advance and the release that must follow it; my frozen launch order names .agent-work/epic-559/c2-generate-the-spine/COMMANDER_RETURN.md as the artifact the Admiral judges completion from, and moving it would take that artifact out from under my principal mid-epic; and this repo's own archive layout shows the EPIC archiving its commanders together at epic closeout (.agent-work/archive/2026-08-09-epic-418-followon/commander-424/), which is the Admiral's act, not mine. c1's actual check is the archive-phase capture gate, and it passes: the episodes are committed and git-tracked, so the record already outlives this worktree, which is the property the move existed to guarantee. Everything else is satisfied on its own terms -- four commits pushed, PR #563 open and titled FINAL with do-not-merge stated, the staged diff carrying no suspicious artifacts, and the lease still held so it covers this entry. The release follows immediately and is the last thing I do.
